dm-quickstart.title: DM quick start
dm-quickstart.summary: From an empty campaign to the first battle.

s0.heading: What this app is
s0.b0: A DM workspace for your own setting: you describe the world (races, skills, units, spells, artifacts), write the scenario, show scenes and run battles. Players play from their phones, and the server calculates the combat rules.

s1.heading: The path to the first battle

b0.i1: Add enemy units, by hand or by import.
b0.i2: Invite players with the invite code.
b0.i3: Approve hero drafts or create heroes yourself.

s1.b1: This same list is the "First steps" checklist on the campaign page; it ticks off completed items on its own.

s2.heading: How to invite players
s2.b0: The invite code is in the "Campaign settings" block on the campaign page. A player enters it on the campaigns page via "Join a campaign".

s3.heading: Hero drafts
s3.b0: A player without a hero creates a draft. It appears in "Characters" marked "pending approval". You approve it and the hero becomes active, or send it back with a comment.
s3.b1: A draft never enters a battle, the balance or the party summary until you approve it.

dm-world.title: Campaign world: races, skills, trees
dm-world.summary: What a hero is made of and how to set up their growth.

s0.heading: Races
s0.b0: A race sets the base stats, the passive ability and the list of skills available to its heroes. Portraits for player drafts are taken from the avatars of that race's units.

s1.heading: Skills and effects
s1.b0: A skill is a set of effects: bonuses to stats and damage, resistances, triggers on battle events, reactions. The battle engine applies them itself, so you don't have to calculate anything by hand.
s1.b1: Races, artifacts, artifact sets and units have the same effects.

s2.heading: Progression trees
s2.b0: A tree is tied to a race: which skills a hero unlocks with levels and in what order. Fill the skill library first, then build the tree.

b0.i0: A hero gets spells through skills and levels; in battle they are cast from the spellbook or from the map.
b0.i1: An artifact is unique: it is held by one hero (equipped or in the stash). Artifacts can be passed between heroes.
b0.i2: Several artifacts from one set give an extra bonus.

s4.heading: Import
s4.b0: Lists of units, skills and other reference data can be imported from JSON with the import button on the list page.

s0.heading: Units and tiers
s0.b0: A unit is a monster or a squad: stats, attacks, spells, abilities. Level and tier determine how strong it is; stronger units have a higher difficulty class on their effects.

s1.heading: How balance works
s1.b0: There is no separate difficulty setting. During preparation and at battle start the app calculates the strength of the player party and adjusts enemy HP and damage so the battle is fair.
s1.b1: Armor class, resistances to damage types and the spells of both sides are taken into account. Summoned creatures are not part of the calculation.

s2.heading: Reserve
s2.b0: Participants can be held in reserve and brought into the battle later: reinforcements, an ambush, a second wave.

dm-battle.title: Running a battle
dm-battle.summary: Scene setup, the map, turns and finishing a battle.

s0.heading: Scene setup
s0.b0: Create a battle in "Battle scenes": sides, heroes, units, the map. A prepared battle waits until you start it; players see the join button in the header only after the start.

s1.heading: Map and modes
s1.b0: The map is a grid with obstacles, walls and weather. Besides the regular mode there is a maze with fog. Obstacles on the line of fire grant cover automatically.

s2.heading: Turns, morale, finishing

b0.i0: You take the units' turns; players take theirs from their phones.
b0.i1: Morale can grant an extra turn or force a skip; the threshold is visible on the card.
b0.i2: When one side wins, the battle waits for your confirmation and shows the result screen.

s2.b1: Every action can be rolled back from the battle log.
s2.b2: A natural 20 and a natural 1 give a critical effect, also on the saving throws of spell targets. Turn on "DM picks crit/fumble effects" in the campaign settings: the player's action pauses and you pick an effect from the list, choose "Random" or cancel the action. Without the option the effect is random.

s3.heading: Battle music
s3.b0: The track library is in "Battle music"; in battle there is a player with a playlist that all participants hear.

dm-scenario-show.title: Scenario and show
dm-scenario-show.summary: The campaign manuscript, slides for players and the curtain.

s0.heading: Manuscript
s0.b0: The scenario is pages with sections: scenes, DM notes, hero biographies. The table of contents is on the left; played scenes collapse.

s1.heading: Links to slides and battles
s1.b0: A scenario row can be linked to a show slide or a battle. The link sits above the row text: the slide is shown with a button or a double click, and the battle opens from the same place.

s2.heading: Show and curtain
s2.b0: "Scene show" is a set of slides with music. You switch slides and players see them in sync.

b1.i1: B for the curtain: players see the chosen curtain slide, and position and music are not reset.
b1.i2: N (in the scenario) for the next row.

dm-ai.title: AI assistant
dm-ai.summary: Your own key, edit proposals and MCP.

s0.heading: Your own key
s0.b0: The assistant runs on your Claude, OpenAI or Gemini key. The key is stored encrypted and is never returned to the browser.

s1.heading: Edit proposals
s1.b0: The assistant never changes the scenario by itself: it proposes edits, and you apply or reject them. A version of the page is saved before applying.

s2.heading: Live mode and images
s2.b0: During play the assistant sees the current scene and show. It can also generate an image for a slide if the key supports it (OpenAI or Gemini).

s3.heading: MCP and API tokens
s3.b0: The same tools are available to external AI clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor) through MCP. A token is created on the campaign's "AI and API" page and shown only once.

dm-world-map.title: World map
dm-world-map.summary: The map editor, hero travel, showing to players and scenario links.

s0.heading: Editor
s0.b0: "World map" in the DM menu: upload a map image, place locations (markers) and draw zones. A marker can lead to a nested map, such as a city inside a continent. Hidden markers and zones are visible only to the DM until you reveal them.

s1.heading: Hero travel
s1.b0: The "Travel" tool moves selected heroes to a point or location. "Enter" takes the party to a nested map, "Exit" brings it back. Every transition is written to the log; you can mark a rest in it, but it doesn't restore resources yet, it is only a record.
s1.b1: The "Through the hero's eyes" switch shows the map the way the chosen hero sees it, with their own fog.

s2.heading: Showing to players
s2.b0: In "Show" or in the scenario dock press "Show map to players", pick a map and, if needed, a marker to focus on. Each player sees only their own fog, and a map unknown to them is open only while it is on screen. "Enter" in the dock's travel switches the show to the nested map with a falling animation.

s3.heading: Notes
s3.b0: In the marker panel you see players' public notes and can delete them. Players' private notes are not visible to you.

s4.heading: Scenario links and mentions
s4.b0: A row or a chapter of the scenario can be linked to a place on the map: a "📍" chip above the text, and the "Show on map" button brings up the map focused on the place. An @Place mention in the text leads to the editor with the marker selected. If the marker was deleted, the chip shows "Place unavailable".

player-quickstart.title: Player quick start
player-quickstart.summary: From the invite code to a ready hero.

s0.heading: How to join
s0.b0: The DM gives you an invite code. On the campaigns page press "Join a campaign" and enter the code; the campaign appears in your list.

s1.heading: Hero draft
s1.b0: Open the campaign and go to "My character". While you have no hero, you create a draft: race, name, stats, portrait and backstory.

b1.i0: Any field can be generated, or everything at once.
b1.i1: The portrait is taken from the race library; if the DM connected AI, it can be drawn.
b1.i2: Stats are the standard array or point-buy; the server checks that everything is fair.

s1.b2: The draft goes to the DM for approval. They can accept it or send it back with a comment, then fix it and submit again.

s2.heading: Hero sheet
s2.b0: After approval "My character" shows the hero sheet with tabs:

b1.i0: "Combat" for stats, attacks, defense and saving throws.
b1.i1: "Abilities" for skills and the progression tree.
b1.i3: "Inventory" for equipment, backpack, money and the log.
b1.i4: "History" for the biography, goals and your personal notes (the DM can't see them).

s2.b2: A new level comes after battles; a level-up marker will appear on the sheet.

s3.heading: Scene show
s3.b0: During play the DM can show slides with music. Open "Show" in the campaign or press the show button in the header, and the scene will switch in sync with the DM.

player-battle.title: Battle from your phone
player-battle.summary: How to move, attack and cast in battle.

s0.heading: How to get into a battle
s0.b0: When the DM starts a battle, a join-battle button appears in the header. There is nothing to install: the battle works in your phone's browser.

s1.heading: Your turn
s1.b0: The turn order is visible at the top. When your turn comes, actions appear:

b1.i0: Move: pick a cell on the map.
b1.i1: Attack: pick a target; the server won't accept targets out of reach.
b1.i2: Spell: from the spellbook or directly from the map.
b1.i3: End turn: the button at the bottom; without it the turn won't pass on.

s2.heading: Attack and spells
s2.b0: The server calculates rolls and damage; you see the result and the animation. For ranged attacks, obstacles on the line of fire give the target cover automatically.
s2.b1: For enemies you see their health state, not exact HP; you learn armor class and traits from attacks.

s3.heading: Morale and conditions
s3.b0: High morale can grant an extra turn, low morale can force a skip. Effects on a hero (poison, stun and so on) are visible on their card; they wear off on their own over the rounds.

s4.heading: When a hero falls
s4.b0: A hero at 0 HP leaves the map but not the game: an ally or the DM can bring them back. After the battle the DM sums up and experience is added to the sheet.

player-world-map.title: World map
player-world-map.summary: Where your heroes are, what is discovered and how to leave notes.

s0.heading: The "Map" tile
s0.b0: A "Map" tile appears on the campaign dashboard once the DM has prepared a map. It shows your heroes and the places they have already discovered; the rest is covered by fog, separate for each player.

s1.heading: Notes on places
s1.b0: Tap a discovered place: the "Shared" tab holds the party's notes, "Mine" holds private ones that only you see. A note can be attached to your hero.

s2.heading: Map on the show screen
s2.b0: When the DM puts a map on the "Show", it opens for you on its own even if you haven't been there; the fog stays yours. When the DM ends the show, the open map is limited again to what you know.

player-acquaintances.title: Acquaintances
player-acquaintances.summary: NPCs your heroes have met, their journal and your notes.

s0.heading: What acquaintances are
s0.b0: The "Acquaintances" tile appears once the DM has opened this section. An acquaintance is an NPC with a name, portrait, description and an encounter journal. It appears as soon as the DM marks the scene where you met them as played; new journal entries work the same way.
s0.b1: A new acquaintance gets a golden "new" mark and a notification; the mark fades when you open the section.

s1.heading: Notes
s1.b0: You can add your own note to every acquaintance. You and the DM can see it; other players cannot. An empty note is removed.

dm-acquaintances.title: Acquaintances
dm-acquaintances.summary: NPCs from the scenario: how to create them, when players see them and how to delete them.

s0.heading: How to create
s0.b0: In the scenario editor, select an NPC's name and press "Acquaintance". Pick a micro NPC (name, description, avatar) or a full NPC from the campaign's characters. The chip in the text leads to the acquaintance card; an @-mention inserts an existing acquaintance instead of creating a duplicate. One character is one acquaintance.
s0.b1: The acquaintance dialog has a journal: add entries and tie them to scenario sections. The tool is unavailable on hero pages: their chapters open separately and never become "played".

s1.heading: When players see them
s1.b0: Players see an acquaintance once the section where it was created is marked as played; a journal entry once its own section is played. The section is enabled with the "Acquaintances are available to players" switch in the campaign settings. You see everything: hidden items are marked "Hidden". Turning the switch on later does not notify players.

s2.heading: Deleting
s2.b0: Removing the chip from the text does not delete the acquaintance. It can only be deleted explicitly, in the acquaintance dialog, after confirmation.

compendium-import.title: Compendium import
compendium-import.summary: How to upload a JSON compendium, read the report and what to do when the import is blocked.

s0.heading: What it is
s0.b0: A compendium is a single JSON file with spells, units, races, classes, items, books and so on. The import moves it into the campaign in one atomic step: everything selected, or nothing. Up to 3 MiB and 2000 selected entries at a time.

b0.i0: File - pick the JSON. Nothing is saved.
b0.i1: Categories - tick what to import; DM materials (books, adventures) are chosen chapter by chapter. Edition and sources are shown here too.
b0.i2: Check - the server builds a report; the campaign is still unchanged. The result is valid for 15 minutes, and any change to the selection or the campaign needs a new check.
b0.i3: Confirm - tick that you have the right to use this file and press "Import".

s2.heading: What to choose
s2.b0: "Recommended" selects the categories the engine understands. Technical categories (images, Foundry) are skipped and not uploaded. If you take only a part, keep the dependencies: spells, feats or classes that other entries refer to must be in the file, the campaign or the SRD.

s3.heading: Reading the report
s3.b0: At the top is "Ready to import" or "Import blocked" plus counters: created, updated, unchanged, errors. Below are coverage by category (mapped, partial, skipped) and the "What next" block with blockers and manual checks.
s3.b1: A manual action means the entry is imported but the engine does not model part of its rules (unit actions, item effects, background equipment and money): set it up in the editor or apply it from the description. It does not block the import.

s4.heading: Classic and 5e 2024 together
s4.b0: Editions are not mixed by default. When a dependency or binding comes from another edition the report warns, and when an explicit binding is needed it blocks the import. Rules are not converted between editions: check the result yourself.

s5.heading: Why the import is blocked
s5.b0: The "Import" button stays disabled while the report has blocking errors. The three most common:

b1.i0: NOTES_SIZE - one entry's notes exceed 64 KB. Shorten the description in the file, untick the matching chapter in "DM materials" or exclude the entry.
b1.i1: UNRESOLVED_REF - an entry needs a dependency (spell, feat, class, race...) that was not found. Add it to the file, bind it to a campaign or SRD record in the dependencies block, or exclude the dependent entry (there is an "Exclude blocked and dependent records and check the rest" button).
b1.i2: MIXED_EDITION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED - a binding between classic and 5e 2024. Press "Allow mixing classic / one and re-check" in the report or tick the matching option in the categories.

s5.b2: After a fix the check reruns automatically or with the "Check JSON" button.
